texts.preamble: Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 1 Page No. 1 To 6 on 13 February, 2012 Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 1 Page In The Court Of Ms. Rachna Tiwari Lakhanpal, Metropolitan Magistrate: Rohini: Delhi Cc U/s. Domestic Violence Deepika Negi
texts.facts: 2. During the course of hearing arguments, only maintenance relief and rent for alternative accommodation were pressed for. 3. Relevant facts for disposal of the application in brief are that complainant was married to the respondent no. 1 on 04.11.2003 at City Banquet Punjabi Bagh. One female child was born out of the said wedlock. Complainant was taunted for not brining adequate dowry at the time of marriage by all the respondents and other family members. Respondent no. 1 got job offer from New Zealand and he left for there in the year 2004 leaving behind the complainant alone. Complainant's parents with great difficulty arranged for the funds to send the complainant to New Zealand. On reaching there respondent no. 1/husband ill treated her and confined her to the house. Complainant's father also visited New Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 2 Page no. 1 to 6 Zealand after retirement. Respondent no. 1 started abusing the father of the complainant from the very moment he reached at the house of the respondent no. 1 and went to the extent of attempting to kill the father of the complainant. But with the intervention of friends and relatives the matter was not reported to the police and complainant made her father leave to friends place for his safety and shortly to India. Thereafter, the complainant came to know that the respondent no. 1/husband had been setting a voice recorder at home during the last week of his father's stay at home. Thereafter, respondent treated the complainant with cruelty. Her health also continued to deteriorate and she had to come to India after about 20 days. Complainant alleged that respondent is a man of means and earning Rs. 30,000/ per month but she has not placed on record any proof of his earnings. Complainant has shown photograph of the Bunglow. It appears Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 1 Page No. 1 To 6 on 13 February, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147495830/ 1 that Bunglow is in posh area of Pune. Respondent has no other liability except to maintain the complainant and her child. Complainant has pressed for relief of maintenance and prayed to provide maintenance of Rs. 2,00,000/ per month towards herself and her minor child. 4. However, on the other hand in his reply respondent had denied all the allegations levelled against them. Respondent submitted that he worked as Assistant Professor at monthly salary of Rs. 12,000/ p.m. only. Then he received a work permit and went to New Zealand for work permit which merely entitled a persons to travel to the country but does not Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 3 Page no. 1 to 6 guarantee him/her a job there. Complainant also joined him in New Zealand in June 2005 after respondent no. 1 was able to sponsor her visit to New Zealand and he obtained "Permanent Residency" in New Zealand on 20.06.05. He further submitted that respondent or his family members never forced complainant to deposit her jewellery in the bank locker at Pune. Respondent no. 2 and his wife travelled to New Zealand and stayed with the complainant for four months in the year 2008. Father of complainant also visited New Zealand on the sponsorship of respondent no. 1. The complainant and her father started mental torture of the respondent no.1 and started to heap all kind of insult upon him and taunted him for not having a proper job. During the stay of complainant's father in New Zealand one night complainant made a call to police and told them that she was afraid of respondent no.1. Respondent further alleged that complainant left his house in New Zealand on 06.08.09 and continued to stay in New Zealand till 28.08.09 with another family. 5. In the present case, the allegations of cruelty and counter allegations cannot be decided at this stage, without appreciating evidence.
texts.arguments: 1. The term "maintenance" is defined in Black's Law Dictionary, (6 th Edn. pp. 95354) as under: "The furnishing by one persons to another, for his or her support, of the means of living, or food, clothing, shelter, etc., particularly where the legal relation of the parties is such that one is bound Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 4 Page no. 1 to 6 to support the other, as between father and child or husband and wife". 2. The work "support as defined in the said Dictionary (P. 1439) reads as under: "That which furnishes a livelihood; a source or means of living; subsistence, sustenance, maintenance, or living. In a broad sense, the term includes all such means of living as should enable one to live in the degree of comfort suitable and becoming to his station of life. It is said to include anything requisite to housing, feeding, clothing, health, proper recreation, vacation, traveling expenses, or other proper cognate purposes; also proper care, nursing and medical attendance in sickness and suitable burial at death". 2. Hon'ble the Supreme Court in "Jasbir Kaur Sehgal vs. District Judge, Dehradun and ors. AIR 1997 SC 3397, observed as under: "No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. The court has to consider the status of the parties, their respective needs, the capacity of the husband to payhaving regard to his Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 5 Page no. 1 to 6 reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he Deepika Negi vs Suhas Singh 1 Page No. 1 To 6 on 13 February, 2012 In this regard Out own High Court in Annurita Vohra vs. Sandeep Vohra - 110(2004) DLT 546, laid down the following principles of law for ascertaining the quantum of maintenance which is as under: "In other words, the court must first arrive at the net disposable income of the husband or the dominant earning spouse. If the other spouse is also working, these earnings must be kept in mind. This would constitute the family resource cake which would then be cutup and distributed amongst the members of the family. The apportionment of the case must be in consonance with the financial requirements of the family members, which is exactly what happens when the spouses are one homogeneous unit". 3. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dr. Kulbhushan Kunwar vs. Raj Kumari - (1971) 2 SCR 672 held that : "Maintenance depends upon a gathering together of all the facts of the situation, the income of the parties, a survey of the conditions and necessities, regard being had to the scale and mode of living, and to the age, habits, wants and class of life of the parties".
